_source: Remaster data for a Phantasie I import from the Amiga copy alone (profile p1-amiga-1.0), applied by the importer (OpenPhantasie.Importer.Pipelines.P1Amiga.P1AmigaTables). Numbers only; no text from the game disk.
_note: Between versions DOS wins over Amiga on numbers (AGENTS.md): an Amiga-only import takes the Amiga's text, maps and names, and DOS I's value in every cell where the Amiga's number differs (reverse-engineering/amiga/GAME-TABLES.md, section 'Amiga vs DOS: numbers'). Every other number of the eleven tables is the same on both disks.
_dos_cells: As phantasie2/apple2-import.json's st_cells (CellPatches): a path into the GameData file the Amiga import builds (DOS shape); a string is an object key, a number an array index, an object picks the array element whose fields match; byte = an offset into a hex string; fog = a map tile whose fog (tile + 120) is kept. A cell holding the Amiga value takes the DOS value; one holding neither is kept and warned.

dos_cells.why: terrain: the Amiga's lake (100) where DOS has mountains (34); user s53 keeps the DOS terrain (amiga/FORMAT.md, Overworld / dungeon map graphics, 'vs DOS')
terrain: the Amiga's lake (100) where DOS has forest (16); user s53 keeps the DOS terrain
fixed fight: the Amiga ships it spent (x8, no fight), DOS live (x7, overworld-movement.md 'tile % 10')
fixed fight: spent on the Amiga, live on DOS
fixed fight: spent on the Amiga, live on DOS
fixed fight: spent on the Amiga, live on DOS
DNG6 cell (14, 35): a jammed lock of bank 2 (0xd6) on the Amiga, of bank 1 (0xc7) on DOS (dungeon-representation.md, Locks)
ORANGE DRAGON's sprite height, the last word of the size table: no sprite height in either program (DOS 22356, Amiga 2570; what reads it is [?], monsters.json _fields sprite_height [~]); DOS's kept
